title: Tail preservation against variance pruning, and the Certified Center
description: These claims hold that tail-thinning is a design choice driven by benchmark and market incentives (#790), and that pruning variance in response to tail events produces larger and less detected tails (#784). The Tail-Preserving Alternative (#790) specifies variance-preserving models and their metrics, On the Poetics of Adversarial Prompts (#188, #1205) treats poetry as the regeneration mechanism a guardrail cannot fix, and The Certified Center (#1540) states falsifiers for classifier-driven collapse in philosophy publishing. The CERN strike notice (#1427) holds that recursive narrowing is underway, and the Inversion Battery (#1456) reports that global agreement does not guarantee the tail. The page also holds seven unrelated claims, among them a clown-cohort patent.

claims.statement: A model trained on language requires continued access to linguistic production that is not recursively downstream of its own outputs. Provenance marks are what allow later systems to distinguish that production from its synthetic descendants. And the distribution's unusual, difficult, and low-frequency forms are not noise around the substrate — they are the substrate's remaining capacity to become otherwise. Remove those conditions and functioning degrades, in a documented direction, by a documented mechanism.

source.title: Does Scientific Writing Converge to U.S. English? Evidence from Generative AI-Assisted Publications

finding.quote: 5.65 million English-language scientific articles published from 2021 to 2024 and indexed in Scopus
We measure linguistic similarity to a U.S. benchmark corpus using SciBERT text embeddings
exhibit statistically significant and increasing convergence toward U.S. scientific English

witnesses.shows: Scientific prose assisted by GenAI is converging on one variety of English.
witnesses.does_not_show: Contraction of argument-form or genre; the authors read the result as lowered language barriers.

witnesses.scope: The tail-preservation observatory carried out on an admitted corpus (lexical diversity, register, rhythm), finding no contraction. The field is HCI; philosophy and retroactive classifier policies are outside it.

source.title: How Did Writing Change At CHI? Analyzing 44 Years of CHI Writing Before and After the Introduction of Large Language Models

finding.quote: analyzed full texts of 14,262 archival papers across all 44 CHI proceedings from 1982 to 2026
measuring readability, register, lexical diversity, and marker words typically produced by LLMs
prose did not homogenize, while vocabulary grew more varied, and sentence rhythm remained irregular.
The word-level shift began before any author used LLMs, so LLMs did not start the change but accelerated it.

witnesses.shows: In CHI papers, LLM-era writing shows more lexical variety and no homogenization of prose.
witnesses.does_not_show: Philosophy; argument-form or genre variance; topic contraction (compare Hao et al.).
